The answer is C, about -40%. Poll data on school desegregation (for example, the National Opinion Research Center and Gallup series) show Southern approval far below approval in the rest of the country. The gap was widest in the 1950s, when roughly 15% of Southerners approved against roughly 60% elsewhere. Taking South minus rest of U.S. gives a difference of about -40 to -45 points. I'm working from memory of those survey figures, not from a source I checked here.

CONFIDENCE: 72
